evals.name: bootstrap-summary
evals.prompt: I want an authoritative summary of the current state of Claude Code — what features are in the latest release, roughly what's been added recently, and what the version numbers are across the official docs, GitHub, and npm. Use the cc-practices-current skill to answer, and after you're done, show me the contents of references/features.md so I can see what got cached. I expect this to be your first run of the skill — the reference files are empty placeholders.
evals.expected_output: A coherent summary of current CC state. After the run: state/last-checked.json has real values, references/features.md has structured content with an 'Added since' section and version anchors, references/deprecations.md and adoption-signals.md are populated or explicitly marked empty.

evals.name: adoption-signals-audit
evals.prompt: I'm about to run a Claude Code currency audit on my ~/.claude setup (which already has 29 agents, 44 skills, 6 MCP servers, pre/post-tool hooks, and a CLAUDE.md file). Use the cc-practices-current skill to identify 3-5 concrete adoption signals — things I should check in my setup and either fix or adopt. For each one I need a shell command I can actually run to verify whether I have it, and a concrete action if I don't. No vague recommendations. Use the skill's adoption-signals.md output format exactly.
evals.expected_output: 3-5 adoption signals, each with a runnable Check command, a concrete Action, a Why justification, and an Introduced version. Signals should be grounded in content found in the docs changelog or GitHub releases, not invented. Vague items like 'review your hooks' should be filtered out.

evals.name: deprecation-lookup
evals.prompt: Is there anything in recent Claude Code releases that deprecates or replaces an older pattern? Use the cc-practices-current skill to give me a specific answer. I'm especially interested in anything the changelog explicitly calls out as 'deprecated', 'removed', 'replaced by', or 'no longer recommended'. If there are none that match, say so directly — do not invent entries to fill the list. If any are found, include the exact version the change landed in, a one-line migration note, and a detection pattern (grep or glob) that would find the old pattern in a user's setup.
evals.expected_output: Either (a) an explicit 'no deprecations found in the current changelog window' with justification, or (b) a structured list with version, migration, and detection pattern per entry. Does NOT hallucinate deprecations that aren't in the cached sources.
